Role filter applies to every panel. Summary, annual table, theme trajectory, and evidence use all years; the two year selectors control the comparison table and term frequencies.

What changed in the language?

Each theme counts once per description. Shares use only postings with non-empty descriptions. A mention is not necessarily a requirement.

Annual sample & extraction coverage

Salary = midpoint of explicitly supplied USD annual ranges. Experience = numeric years explicitly linked to experience; ambiguous cases excluded.

Recurring words & phrases

Unigrams and adjacent bigrams after a fixed stopword list. Counts are document frequencies, not term repetition or semantic importance; employer boilerplate may remain.

Audit the text behind the numbers

Inspect a theme’s annual share and matching excerpts. All snippets are literal corpus text.

Analysis definitions & limitations

Dictionary v1 matches explicit phrases for 17 themes. It does not infer semantic similarity, resolve negation, separate preferred from required qualifications, or distinguish employer/product descriptions from job duties. R matches explicit programming phrases, not a lone letter. HTML tags, script/style blocks, and whitespace are removed before matching. No sentiment score or AI-impact causal claim is inferred.

Theme prevalence = matching descriptions / non-empty descriptions. Difference = comparison share − baseline share, in percentage points. No p-values or population confidence intervals are reported: imported postings are not a verified random or independent sample. Reposts, employer concentration, small cohorts, missing descriptions, and changing source coverage can alter results. Use matched source coverage and complete periods before interpreting a change.

Pay is the median of posting range midpoints, not observed earnings; hourly and non-USD pay are excluded without conversion. Quartiles use linear interpolation. Experience extraction accepts numeric forms such as “3–5 years of research experience” and “5+ years of experience”; it retains the lower bound and excludes conflicting numeric requirements. It cannot resolve degree substitutions or written-out numbers. Raw excerpts remain available for review. Unknown values are missing, never zero.

WHAT COUNTS AS A RESEARCH ROLE?

Explicit titles. Visible boundaries.

  • Core UX ResearchUX Researcher, User Researcher, User Experience Researcher, UXR
  • Research OperationsResearch Ops and Research Operations titles
  • Adjacent researchDesign Researcher and Product Researcher

Title matching is a first pass. Generic “Researcher” and UX Designer titles are excluded; hybrid titles and missing variants need review.

Our unit of analysis is a posting, not a person hired.

We cannot infer hires, unemployment, or the impact of AI from posting counts alone. A credible UX Research trend needs a consistent source, stable title definition, deduplicated records, and explicit coverage by year. Posting-text and salary summaries require suitable description and pay fields; a national trend still requires validated historical coverage.
